nodes.action: deployed without running the test suite
the regression reached every user and forced a full rollback
set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests
no backdoor account was left exposed
adopted a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. You look like you've been up all night.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Because I have. The 2 AM deploy — the one you pushed without running the test suite — broke the login flow for every user. We had to do a full rollback at 3:30.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Oh god. I'm so sorry. I was rushing to get the feature out before the demo, and I skipped the tests. I thought it was a small change.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Small change, huge regression. It hit every single account. We're lucky we caught it before the morning rush, but the damage is done — support tickets are flooding in.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I take full responsibility. I'm going to set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests. No exceptions, even for me.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's a good start. But honestly, we need to talk about the password storage too. I saw the logs — you stored plaintext passwords in the dev database.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Wait, what? No, that was a temporary script for local testing. I never pushed that to production.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: You didn't push it, but the script was still running on the staging server. Three user accounts got compromised before we killed it.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Jesus. I'm so sorry. I'll remove those debug credentials from production right now, and I'll audit every environment for any leftover backdoors.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Please do. And after that, we need a stricter policy — not just for tests, but for the deployment window. No more 2 AM pushes without a checklist.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Agreed. I'll draft that policy today. And I'll make sure untested code never reaches production again — the CI gate will enforce it.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw your CI gate is live. Nice work — it blocked my own merge this morning because I forgot a unit test.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Ha, sorry about that. But that's the point. It's already caught two other PRs. No more untested code slipping through.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. And I checked the production logs — no backdoor account left exposed. You cleaned up all the debug credentials?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Every single one. I also rotated all the API keys and forced a password reset for the affected users. They've been notified.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's solid. Now, about the deployment window — I saw you scheduled the next release for 6 AM on Saturday. Off-peak, but not the middle of the night.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, I figured 6 AM gives us the whole day to monitor if something breaks, and it's still low traffic. Plus, the new policy requires a second pair of eyes on every deploy.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I like it. And that stricter policy — does it cover the deployment window itself? Like, no deploys after 4 PM on Fridays?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. It covers the window, the test requirement, and the rollback plan. I'll send you the doc for review.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Just read your policy doc. It's thorough. I especially like the part about mandatory smoke tests after every deploy.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Thanks. I learned my lesson the hard way. That regression that hit everyone — I never want that again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And the password hashing requirement — that's non-negotiable now, right? No more plaintext anywhere, even in dev.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Correct. I've already updated the dev environment to use the same hashing library as prod. And I added a lint rule that fails if anyone tries to store a raw password.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. So, to recap: CI gate blocks merges without tests, untested code never reaches production, deployments are scheduled for off-peak hours, and no debug credentials or backdoors exist.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: That's the new normal. And the stricter policy covers the deployment window too — so no more 2 AM surprises.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: I'm impressed, Joanna. You turned a disaster into a solid process. Let's grab coffee and celebrate — after you run the test suite, of course.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Deal. And I'll bring the rollback runbook I wrote, just in case.
